scenario.on_this_estate: DESIGN.json specifies unlisted_file as a silent skip and pins no_generated_layer / no_resident_runtime. The live catalog already records the measured class 'skill exists in repo but not in live directory'. The procedure below executes that DESIGN rule.
procedure: 1. Write estate fixture: MANIFEST.json lists capabilities/skills/listed.skill.json only.
2. Place capabilities/skills/orphan.skill.json on disk with id=skill.orphan, not listed.
3. Run the [REDACTED] loader (DESIGN unlisted_file): ok=true, errors=[], warnings=[], loaded_ids=[skill.listed], silent_omission_ids=[skill.orphan].
4. Observe silent loss: skill.orphan is enabled JSON on disk and is not loaded; no error is raised.
5. Run the [REDACTED] completeness gate on the same tree: it FAIL-CLOSES and names skill.orphan.
6. Repair: add the orphan path to MANIFEST.json. Re-run [REDACTED]: both ids load. Re-run [REDACTED]: ok=true.
scenario.title: Unlisted on-disk skill is silently omitted under [REDACTED]; [REDACTED] completeness fails closed

legacy_root.strongest_surviving_counterargument: [REDACTED]'s silent skip of unlisted files is the twin of fail-closed-on-unknown-activation. A [REDACTED] or directory-scanning runtime that auto-promotes orphans would execute unreviewed capabilities (the extra MCP mount / wildcard-hook class). On a single-owner estate, omitting an unlisted skill is cheaper than silently activating one. So [REDACTED] remains lower activation risk even though this unit shows it is not lower omission risk. The surviving claim: [REDACTED] minimises surprise execution, not surprise absence. That claim is correctly scoped and is CONFIRMED by DESIGN; the min-risk claim is not.
